sections.h2: Which Highland County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work in Hillsboro. The county auditor values property and keeps the tax list, the treasurer bills and collects, and the recorder files the deeds that change the owner of record. The auditor's own description calls the auditor the county's chief fiscal officer and the statutory appraiser-in-chief of all real estate, and says the auditor also distributes collected tax to villages, townships and school districts.

sections.h2: How does Highland County value a home for tax?
sections.html:
The auditor's FAQ states that revaluations occur every three years, and that tax value in Ohio is 35% of the appraised market value. The bill then applies the millage rate for the school district, township or village and levies where the parcel sits.

Highland County's parcels sit in several districts. The county's own list names five school districts: Bright Local, Fairfield Local, Greenfield Exempted, Hillsboro City and Lynchburg-Clay Local. Two neighbors on the same road can pay different rates if a district line divides them, so look up the parcel rather than relying on a nearby sale.

The auditor's page reports 32,381 parcels in 2024 across a county of 553 square miles. The Census Bureau counts 19,196 housing units there, so parcels outnumber housing units by a wide margin, which points to farmland, woodland and vacant lots. Rural sellers in particular should read the current agricultural use section below.

sections.h2: When are Highland County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The treasurer's page listed the 2026 real estate dates as March 13 for the first half and August 7 for the second half. Both dates are in the past, so a seller who closed after them should confirm with the treasurer that each half posted as paid. Dates change from year to year, and the treasurer's page is the place to check the next ones.

Owners can pay online through the link on the treasurer's page or by calling the toll-free number it gives, 1-844-920-3600. The mailing address is P.O. Box 824, Hillsboro, OH 45133, and the office phone is 937-393-9951.

Delinquent taxes are a matter for the same office. The auditor's tools menu includes a Delinquency Report, and the Highland County Treasurer can explain what an unpaid balance would add if a sale is pending. A buyer's title company will ask for a payoff either way.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Highland County valuation?
sections.html:
A valuation complaint goes to the county auditor and is heard by the Board of Revision. Under section 5715.19, the complaint must be filed by March 31 of the following tax year or the date the first-half collection closes, whichever is later. A complaint also has to state the amount of overvaluation or undervaluation it claims.

The auditor's forms page lists the paperwork:

  • DTE 1, a complaint against the valuation of real property.
  • DTE 1M, the same complaint for a manufactured or mobile home taxed like real property.
  • DTE 2, a complaint against an assessment other than market value.

The statute also lets an owner pay on the claimed value while a complaint is pending, and it requires the complainant to hand the board the evidence within the owner's knowledge. A recent arm's length sale is the strongest proof, and the county's sales report on the auditor's site shows what nearby parcels sold for.

sections.h2: What tax breaks does Highland County list for owners?
sections.html:
The auditor's forms page groups the relief applications by type. Homestead forms include DTE 105A for senior citizens, disabled persons and surviving spouses, DTE 105I for disabled veterans and surviving spouses, and DTE 105K for surviving spouses of public service officers killed in the line of duty. Owner occupancy applications include DTE 105C for real property and DTE 56 for manufactured and mobile homes. Highland County's auditor can give the filing window and any income or age limits that apply, because those change by tax year.

Destroyed or damaged property has its own form, DTE 26, and there are exemption applications for qualifying owners such as veterans' and fraternal organizations. Check the auditor's site before assuming a form applies.

The Highland County Auditor's agricultural page covers the current agricultural use valuation program, which taxes qualifying farmland on income value instead of market value. Land with 10 or more acres, not counting the homesite, qualifies when used exclusively for agriculture. Smaller land qualifies if it earned gross income of at least $2,500 in each of the past three years. The initial application costs $25 and must be filed before the first Monday in March.

sections.h2: What happens to tax savings when a farm is sold in Highland County?
sections.html:
Land that leaves the agricultural program owes a recoupment charge equal to three years of the tax savings. The county's FAQ says that applies when the owner fails to reapply or when a change in use means the land is no longer devoted exclusively to agriculture.

The sale paperwork covers it too. Section 319.202 requires the buyer's statement to say whether the parcel was in the program, and the auditor's forms list DTE 102 for a conveyance of that kind of property and DTE 101 for homestead property. A farm seller should ask the auditor for the likely recoupment before listing, because the number may affect the price a buyer will pay.

Woodland has a similar choice. The county's FAQ says timber land cannot claim savings under both the agricultural program and the older forestry law, and that a program application for woodland needs a forest management plan prepared by a licensed forester and approved by the auditor.

sections.h2: What does Highland County look like to a home seller?
sections.html:
Highland County covers about 553 square miles of hilly land around Hillsboro, its county seat and largest city. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts shows a 2025 population estimate of 43,823, a 74.3% owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied value of $168,900 for 2020 to 2024, and a median household income of $65,785. About 14.6% of residents live in poverty, and the average commute is 29.1 minutes.

The county reports 733 employer establishments, with employment up 4.9% from 2022 to 2023. Health care and social assistance receipts reached about $195 million in 2022. A buyer's lender will look at the same numbers, which helps explain why an accurate tax estimate matters at listing.

Sellers behind on payments can start with the treasurer, then ask the auditor for the parcel's tax history before talking to a buyer. The recorder and auditor share the 119 Governor Foraker Place address, so a deed, a lien search and a valuation question can be handled in one visit.

faqs.q: Who sends the Highland County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Highland County Treasurer bills and collects the tax. The office is at P.O. Box 824 in Hillsboro, the phone is 937-393-9951, and payments can also be made online.

faqs.q: What fraction of market value is taxed in Highland County?
faqs.a: 35%. The auditor's FAQ states that Ohio tax value is 35% of appraised market value, with revaluations every three years.

faqs.q: When can I file a complaint against my valuation?
faqs.a: By March 31 of the following tax year, or the date the first-half collection closes if that is later. File with the Highland County Auditor on form DTE 1, and the Board of Revision hears it.

faqs.q: Does Highland County have farmland tax relief?
faqs.a: Yes, the current agricultural use valuation program. It applies to land used exclusively for agriculture, with a $25 initial application due before the first Monday in March.

faqs.q: Do I owe anything extra if farmland leaves the program?
faqs.a: Yes, a recoupment charge equal to the tax savings of the last three years. Ask the auditor for an estimate before you sign a purchase contract.
